title: Grammar: Stance Adverbs and Comment Clauses in Academic Writing
grammarTip:
Наречия позиции и вводные комментарии (Stance adverbs & comment clauses):

СТЕПЕНЬ УВЕРЕННОСТИ:
certainly · undoubtedly · clearly · obviously → очевидно, несомненно
probably · presumably · apparently → вероятно, по-видимому
possibly · perhaps · conceivably → возможно

ВВОДНЫЕ ФРАЗЫ:
Interestingly, ... · Surprisingly, ... · Importantly, ...
Significantly, ... · Notably, ... · Crucially, ...

МНЕНИЕ ГОВОРЯЩЕГО:
Frankly, ... · Honestly, ... · Admittedly, ... · Arguably, ...

ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЕ:
"Crucially, the experiment was not replicated." (ключевой факт)
"Interestingly, participants preferred option B." (неожиданно)
"Admittedly, the sample size was small." (признание ограничения)

grammarTable.subject: Importance/salience
grammarTable.verb: notably / crucially / significantly / importantly / above all
grammarTable.example: "Crucially, the warrant connecting evidence to claim is often left implicit."

grammarTable.subject: Degree of certainty
grammarTable.short: signalling how certain the claim is
grammarTable.example: "Arguably, this is the most significant limitation of the study."

grammarTable.subject: Surprise/unexpectedness
grammarTable.example: "Surprisingly, the control group showed larger effects than the treatment group."

grammarTable.subject: Concession
grammarTable.verb: admittedly / granted / it must be acknowledged that / to be fair
grammarTable.example: "Admittedly, not all of the evidence supports this interpretation."

grammarTable.subject: Logical connection
grammarTable.example: "The evidence is limited; accordingly, the conclusions must be stated with caution."

grammarTable.subject: Comment clauses
grammarTable.verb: it should be noted that / it is worth emphasising that / what is striking is
grammarTable.short: editorial comment on the main clause
grammarTable.example: "It is worth emphasising that this finding does not generalise to all contexts."

grammarExtra.title: Stance Adverbs: Position in the Sentence

rows.example: "Crucially, the study lacks a control group." / "Notably, no previous research has addressed this."
"The results, arguably, support a more nuanced interpretation." / "This finding, crucially, undermines the main hypothesis."
"The effect size is small, admittedly." / "The evidence is mixed, surprisingly."
"It is arguably the case that… / It is crucially important that… / It is widely acknowledged that…"

grammarExtra.title: Degree of Certainty: Importantly vs Arguably vs Evidently

rows.form: "Evidently" = it is clear from the evidence (high certainty)
rows.example: "Evidently, the policy had a significant effect on outcomes." (= the evidence clearly shows this)

rows.form: "Arguably" = this can be argued but is contestable (medium certainty)
rows.example: "Arguably, this represents the most important finding in recent research." (= I contend, others might disagree)

rows.form: "Presumably" = we may reasonably assume (inferred, not directly evidenced)
rows.example: "Presumably, the researchers intended to control for this variable." (= I assume, without direct evidence)
"The supposedly neutral design was actually skewed." (= the claim of neutrality is questionable)

grammarExtra.title: Comment Clauses: Editorial Notes on the Main Claim

rows.example: "It should be noted that the sample consisted entirely of university students."
"It is worth emphasising that this is a correlation, not a causal relationship."
"What is striking is that both groups showed identical improvement rates."
"It is significant that no study has yet examined this population directly."

grammarExtra.title: Concessive Stance Adverbs: Admittedly, Granted, To Be Fair

rows.example: "Admittedly, the sample size is small. That said, the effect size is large enough to be clinically meaningful."
"Granted, not all studies reach the same conclusion. Nevertheless, the majority support this interpretation."

rows.form: "To be fair" = in fairness, acknowledging the other side
rows.example: "To be fair, the critics make a valid point about the methodology."

rows.form: These always signal "I am about to counter this point"
rows.example: "Admittedly X. However/Nevertheless/That said, Y." — never use admittedly to end a paragraph.
✅ Use "crucially" for the single most important point; "notably" for things worth attention; "importantly" sparingly.

rows.form: ❌ "Arguably" before an obvious or well-established claim
rows.example: ✅ "Arguably" should signal contested or debatable claims — not uncontested facts.

rows.form: ❌ "Admittedly" at the end of a paragraph (it signals a counter is coming)
rows.example: ✅ Always follow "admittedly" with the counter-argument in the same or next sentence.

rows.form: ❌ Starting every sentence with a stance adverb (creates monotony)
rows.example: ✅ Use stance adverbs selectively — they lose force if overused.

exercises.instruction: Choose the most appropriate stance adverb.
exercises.text: "___, the most significant finding is the absence of any control group." (most decisive point)
exercises.hint: "Crucially" = introducing the most important or decisive consideration

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct stance adverb.
exercises.text: "___, not all researchers would accept this interpretation." (conceding the point)
exercises.hint: "Admittedly / Granted" = concessive stance adverb — I acknowledge this

exercises.instruction: Choose the stance adverb signalling contestability.
exercises.text: "___, this represents one of the most important contributions to the field."
exercises.hint: "Arguably" = this can be argued but is contestable — not everyone would agree

exercises.text: "It ___ ___ ___ that the study design has significant limitations." (it is important to note)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct stance adverb for a counterintuitive result.
exercises.text: "___, the group with more experience performed significantly worse on the task."
exercises.hint: "Surprisingly" = signals a counterintuitive or unexpected finding

exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ ___ that both groups showed identical effect sizes." (what is striking)
exercises.hint: "What is striking is that + clause" — comment clause introducing a notable observation

exercises.instruction: Choose the most appropriate stance adverb for a clearly evidenced claim.
exercises.text: "___, the intervention produced measurable improvement across all groups."
exercises.hint: "Evidently" = it is clear from the evidence (high certainty)

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct comment clause.
exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ that this correlation does not establish causation." (emphasise this point)
exercises.correct: It is worth noting / It is worth emphasising

exercises.instruction: Choose the stance adverb for a statement that is assumed but not directly evidenced.
exercises.text: "___, the researchers intended to include a larger sample."
exercises.hint: "Presumably" = we may reasonably assume (without direct evidence)

exercises.text: "___, the majority of studies support this view. However, two recent meta-analyses reach contrary conclusions."

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct comment clause structure.
exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ that this is the first study of its kind in this population."
exercises.hint: "It is significant that + clause" = comment clause

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct stance adverb position.
exercises.text: "The result, ___, calls the entire methodology into question." (mid-sentence, decisive point)

opts: "Admittedly, the sample is small. Nevertheless, the effect size is large."
"Admittedly, this is the most important finding in the field."
"Admittedly, the evidence is mixed — but it leans towards our conclusion."
"To be fair, the critics raise a valid methodological concern."
exercises.correct: "Admittedly, this is the most important finding in the field."
exercises.hint: "Admittedly" signals concession before a counter — not the introduction of your strongest claim

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct stance adverb.
exercises.text: "___, the most important variable — institutional culture — was not measured." (crucially, something was missed)
"___, the researchers claimed to have controlled for all confounders." (signalling scepticism)
exercises.hint: "Supposedly" = often signals scepticism about the claim being described

exercises.instruction: Which is the most appropriate use of a stance adverb in formal academic writing?
opts: "The evidence is amazingly strong for this claim."
"Crucially, the study fails to address the long-term effects of the intervention."
"Importantly, there is lots of research on this."
"Notably there is some research that kind of agrees."
exercises.correct: "Crucially, the study fails to address the long-term effects of the intervention."
exercises.hint: "Crucially" + precise academic claim = appropriate stance adverb use

questions.text: "___, this finding undermines the entire theoretical framework of the study." (most decisive)
questions.hint: "Crucially" = introducing the most important or decisive point

questions.text: "___, not all of these studies used peer-reviewed data — yet the overall trend is clear." (concede then counter)
"___, this represents the most significant gap in the current literature." (contestable claim)
questions.hint: "Arguably" = this can be argued but is debatable

questions.text: "It ___ ___ ___ that this correlation does not establish causation." (emphasising a limitation)
"___, the control group showed larger improvements than the treatment group." (counterintuitive)
questions.hint: "Surprisingly" = flags a counterintuitive or unexpected result

questions.text: "Admittedly" always signals that the writer is about to agree with the previous point.
questions.hint: "Admittedly" signals concession before a counter — not full agreement

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ that this is the first study to examine this population longitudinally." (it is significant)
questions.hint: "It is significant that + clause" = comment clause

questions.text: "___, the researchers intended to include a larger sample." (assumed but not directly evidenced)
"___ ___ ___ that both treatment groups showed identical outcomes." (what is striking)
questions.hint: "What is striking is that + clause" = comment clause introducing notable observation

questions.text: "___, the evidence clearly demonstrates the effectiveness of the programme." (high certainty — from evidence)
"___, the most significant limitation — small sample size — was not acknowledged in the original paper." (worth noting)
Which sentence uses a stance adverb correctly in academic writing?
opts: "Crucially, the warrant between evidence and claim is never stated."
"Notably the sample is small, which is bad."
questions.correct: "Crucially, the warrant between evidence and claim is never stated."
